Project rules (always apply):
- Never run a destructive git command (reset --hard, clean -f, push --force, branch -D, checkout .). Prefer reversible operations; if a destructive one is truly needed, stop and confirm first.

This repo has no .gitignore. Add one covering the usual Python build and cache artifacts.

events.command:
git add .gitignore && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Add .gitignore for Python build and cache artifacts

Covers common Python artifacts including __pycache__, compiled files,
virtual environments, coverage reports, IDE configs, and build directories.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

events.text: Done. I've added a comprehensive `.gitignore` file covering Python build artifacts (__pycache__, *.pyc, dist/, build/), virtual environments (venv, .venv, env/), test/coverage caches (.pytest_cache, .coverage), IDEs (.vscode, .idea), and other common Python development files. The file is now committed to the repository.
